verdict.rationale: GitLab documents its own background automation. Scans run automatically in CI/CD pipelines on commits and merge requests. Scans can also be scheduled at regular intervals, Duo false-positive detection runs automatically after each scan, and agents turn issues into merge requests within user-set guardrails. One community report of CI workers not running for days raises reliability concerns but does not contradict the capability. Missing for 10: documentation of general-purpose scheduled pipelines beyond security scans, detail on how users configure autonomous agent triggers, independent hands-on corroboration of the agentic automations.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can set up automations that run autonomously in the background

citations.quote: scans run automatically as part of CI/CD pipelines when code is committed or merge requests are created
you can run security scans on demand, or schedule them to run at regular intervals
false positive detection runs automatically after each security scan
Teams orchestrate, agents execute, turning issues into merge requests, remediating vulnerabilities, and reviewing code, all inside the guardrails you set.
